title: 16 strategies tested, 15 buried, 0 sold. My rules, written down so you can hold me to them.
author: Ok_Map5721
selftext:
Every week there's a new "my bot made X%" post here. And every week someone asks the obvious question in the comments: why should I believe any of this?

Honestly, it's a fair question. So here's my answer for my own stuff, written down in public so I can't quietly change it later.

Quick background. I'm not a fund and I'm not selling anything. I've spent a long time testing ideas on crypto, forex and commodities. 16 so far, 15 dead, no real money lost. Most of what I post here is the graveyard, because that's where the useful lessons are.

And I've learned I'm really good at fooling myself. I had a t-stat of 16.9 that turned into 1.28 once I fixed how I was sampling. I had a slippage number I typed into a config and never checked, and it was off by 5.5x. I had a London session "pattern" on EUR/USD that fell apart the moment I tried it on GBP/USD. So none of the rules below are me being some kind of saint. They're me not trusting myself.

\*\*1. Write it down before looking.\*\*  
What I'm testing, why it should work at all, what data, what counts as a pass. Saved and hashed before anything runs. If I don't know why something should work, I don't get to be impressed when it does.

\*\*2. Count everything I tried.\*\*  
Including the stuff I dropped after five minutes, and every idea an AI threw at me. If I looked at 40 things, the winner gets judged as one of 40.

\*\*3. Measure costs, don't guess them.\*\*  
Fees from the exchange, spread and slippage from the real order book. Not testnet, the spread there was 11x the real one when I checked.

\*\*4. Know what the test can actually see.\*\*  
Before running it, I work out the smallest effect it could detect. If that's bigger than my costs, a "no edge" result means nothing. 7 of my first 12 "no edge" conclusions turned out to be exactly that.

\*\*5. Feed it garbage first.\*\*  
Random entries, shuffled returns. If my pipeline lets noise through, its passes are worthless.

\*\*6. Touch the holdout once.\*\*  
At the end. If I peek and tweak, it stops being a holdout and I have to admit that.

\*\*7. Post what dies.\*\*  
With numbers. That's most of what I have, and it's probably the most useful part anyway.

And one rule just for this sub: I'm never going to ask anyone here for money, or sell a course, a signal group, a bot or a strategy pack. If I ever find something that holds up, the first thing you'll see won't be a pitch. It'll be months of live results with real fills, checked against what I wrote down beforehand. If someone (me included) shows up without that, ignore them.

That's the deal. If you think one of these rules is too soft or I'm missing something obvious, tell me. Rather fix it now than find the hole later.

If you want to see the next ones as they come out, hit follow on my profile. That's the easiest way not to miss them.

comments.author: AoideusWasBanned
comments.body:
The t-stat going from 16.9 to 1.28 after fixing sampling is the most useful line in the post. My guess is overlapping windows, if you take a forward return every bar the neighbouring samples share most of their data and the t-stat explodes. Might be worth adding as a written rule: non-overlapping samples or Newey-West errors, nothing else counts.

Also respect for checking power. 7 of 12 "no edge" results being underpowered is something almost nobody looks at, most of those are really "not enough trades to tell" and people bury ideas that never got a fair test.

replies.author: Ok_Map5721
replies.body:
Spot on, it was exactly that. 12-hour forward returns sampled every 5 minutes, so neighbouring rows shared almost the whole window and the same move got counted over a hundred times.

Good call on making it a written rule, I'm adding it as #8: non-overlapping samples or Newey-West/HAC errors with the lag set to the horizon, nothing else counts. And a rough sanity check before any of that: effective sample size is about N divided by the horizon in bars. If that number is small, no error correction will rescue it.

And yes on the power point, "not enough trades to tell" getting read as "doesn't work" is how good ideas get buried. It cuts the other way too, though. An underpowered test that happens to come back positive is just as meaningless, and that's the one people actually trade.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: the slippage number typed into a config and never checked, I'd bet half this sub has one sitting there right now. and counting the ideas a chatbot threw at you as tries is the rule almost nobody keeps, it's so easy to call those free.

replies.author: Ok_Map5721
replies.body: Ha, probably more than half. The AI-ideas one is sneaky because it doesn't feel like trying, it feels like brainstorming. But every idea you actually looked at counts, whether it came from your head or a chatbot.
